# MonoSchemes UI

> MonoSchemes monochrome React design system — semantic tokens, accessible components, and light, dark, and inverse themes.

## Start building

- [Consumer README](README.md): installation, stylesheet, themes, and fonts.
- [Agent instructions](docs/agent-package/AGENTS.md): component selection, usage rules, accessibility, themes, and validation.
- [Application recipes](docs/agent-package/recipes.md): login, settings, filtered dashboard, landing page, detail page (with `DescriptionList`), multi-step form, and view states.
- [Component-to-Figma map](src/tokens/components.json): component names, Figma node references, props, and agent guidance.
- [Figma Community kit](https://www.figma.com/community/file/1706316593970846496/monoschemes-monochrome-ui-kit): the published Figma file with the same components and tokens, plus visual documentation and examples.
- [TypeScript declarations](dist/index.d.ts): authoritative React API and prop types.

## Core rules

- Import `@monoschemes/ui/style.css` once.
- Use the provided React components and semantic CSS variables; do not invent tokens, colors, component names, or props.
- Set the page theme on `<html>` with `data-theme="light"` or `data-theme="dark"`.
- Use `data-theme="inverse"` for a contrasting region that must adapt to either page theme. Do not nest inverse regions.
- Keep component styling in the library. Use consumer CSS for layout and responsive composition.
- Load Inter and JetBrains Mono in the consuming app; the package does not bundle these fonts.
